column1: # source: WRITTEN FROM KNOWLEDGE, not extracted from any book or database. Each row is a compound recipe (head + modifier = target) that real languages use for the target meaning, after: Urban 2012 (Analyzability and Semantic Associations in Referring Expressions: a study in comparative lexicology, PhD Leiden; complex lexemes for 160 meanings in a 78-language sample, e.g. 'bark' = 'tree skin', 'sun' = 'eye of day', 'spring' = 'water eye', 'fruit' = 'tree child'); Brown 1976 and Witkowski & Brown 1978/1985 on body-part partonomy and plant life-forms; Brown 1999 (Lexical Acculturation in Native American Languages, Oxford: introduced animals and plants named 'big dog' = horse, 'foreign X' / 'X-like native analog'); Witkowski & Brown 1983 (marking reversals); Buck 1949 (A Dictionary of Selected Synonyms in the Principal Indo-European Languages); Haspelmath & Tadmor 2009 (WOLD 'analyzable' words); the generic + specific compounds of Mainland Southeast Asia (Thai nók-X 'bird-X', plaa-X 'fish-X', tôn-X 'tree-X'; Malay pohon X, burung X; Mandarin song-shu 'pine-tree', li-yu 'carp-fish'; Enfield 2003, Bisang 1999) and English reindeer < Old Norse hreinn + deer.

# version: hand-authored 2026-11-04 (procedural-language lane, compounds and shifts round); extended 2026-11-07 (round 5: recipes for the WOLD meanings added to concepts.tsv: kin by birth order and marriage, body parts, weather, time, house)
# licence: original text for this repository (no third-party data copied); cite the works above when using it.

# CLICS3: at load time lexicon.py joins each (target, head) and (target, modifier) pair with data/clics_edges.tsv; a pair CLICS3 also attests as a colexification in >= 3 families (BARK/SKIN 49, MILK/BREAST 26, MOON/SUN 18 ...) adds family count / 10 to the weight (a motivated compound is often a colexification too).

# columns: target = the concept named; head = the semantic category the target is a kind (or a part) of: 'tree SKIN' for bark, 'day EYE' for sun, 'mountain ROAD' for a pass, 'woman CHILD' for a girl; modifier = the word that says which one ('SELF' = the target's own current word: a generic + specific renewal, Thai plaa-X, English rein-deer); weight = typicality 1 (attested, uncommon) .. 3 (common across families); example = one or two real cases (romanized) or the source.

# Only these recipes make compounds (lexicon.compound); a target with no row is renewed by derivation, shift, a loan or a fresh root instead. Elaborations (lexicon.ELABORATIONS: MILK + SOUR = soured milk) and function-word reinforcement (data/derivations.tsv 'reinforce' rows) are separate tables.
